summary: Martin Lehnert is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Freiburg. He served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal specializes in religious and Buddhist studies, having studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He has held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt (1948–2014) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1974–1980) and Heidelberg University (~1980–1987). He held a faculty post at the University of Chicago from around 1990 to 2014.
Martin Seeger works in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD under Barend Jan Terwiel at the University of Hamburg by 2004, where he also held an academic post attested that same year.

Martin T. Adam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes (attested 2002). He also studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies under Kameshwar Nath Mishra (1998–1999).

Martin Willson (1946–2005) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His education included training under traditional teachers Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under MA supervisor Lambert Schmithausen and received her Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna (attested 2012). She also held a post at the University of Vienna.
Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and mentor Ester Bianchi (attested 2015).
Maruo Ujiie is a Buddhist studies scholar who engaged in research study at Tribhuvan University, attested in 1970. In 1970, he also held an attested post as a lecturer at Koyasan University.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a long-term academic appointment at the University of Michigan from around 1949 to 1993.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a scholar of sinology and history. She studied at Vassar College (~1934–1938), Radcliffe College (~1938–1951), and Harvard University (~1938–1951), and held a post at Yale University from around 1959 to 1970.
Mary Jaksch (1947–) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007).

Marybeth White works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a double major honors degree at York University and became a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and sinology who studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra. She served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a sinologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953). He later held posts at Otani University (~1993–2000) and Kyoto University as professor emeritus (~1993–2015).

Masaaki Hattori (1924–) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta. He spent decades at Kyoto University, eventually becoming professor emeritus (~1987), and held visiting posts at Toronto, Berkeley, and Vienna.

Masaaki Nitta (1936–) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1961–1966). He held professor posts at Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1983–1988) and Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1991).

Masaaki Nohin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (attested 1999–2003) and as a professor (attested 2013–2014).
Masaaki Tsuchiya (1960–) is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1980–1989) and held a post at Senshu University around 1999.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Kiel, and under Friedrich Max Müller and Paul Deussen. A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, he became professor of religious studies at Tokyo (1904) and lectured at Collège de France.
